# Federal Reserve and Independent Agencies

## By the end of today

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
You will be able to explain why some government power is insulated from short-term politics, and what trade-offs that insulation creates.
:::

## Where this fits

The executive implements policy.

Some implementation is deliberately placed **outside** ordinary presidential control.

## Cold open

Watch: Sloan Sabbith on the debt ceiling (*The Newsroom*).

[Primary clip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gj5-G01iRyk)

Then a short real clip: Jamie Dimon on default as a “moral disaster.”

## What the fight is really about

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Full faith and credit is a public good. Brinkmanship taxes it.
:::

## Institutions first

Douglass North: credible commitment is a development technology.

Governments that reliably pay their debts make long-term investment rational.

## Bank of England, 1694

After the Glorious Revolution, a government that could be trusted to pay borrowed more cheaply.

That is an institution, not a slogan.

## Trade-off in one line

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Using the ceiling as leverage is meant to force discipline. The debate itself raises borrowing costs.
:::

## Better Angels reminder

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.5em;"}
Rule of law, secure property, and predictable public finance underwrite long-run peace and prosperity.
:::

They are not optional scenery.

## Why a Federal Reserve

Lender of last resort after repeated panics.

Elastic currency.

A bank for the government that is not simply the President’s checking account.

## Dual mandate

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.7em;"}
Maximum employment and stable prices.
:::

## Independence — the design

Congress sets the goals.

The Fed chooses day-to-day means.

Governors: 14-year staggered terms.

## Independent *within* government

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Not a fourth branch. Created by Congress. Oversight remains.
:::

## Same logic as courts

Insulate some decisions from the next election.

Different tools: 14-year terms, not life tenure.

## Grain of truth

- Regional banks and member-bank stock exist
- Jekyll Island was secretive
- Policy mistakes are real

## Then the rest

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
None of that equals a private family owning the money supply.
:::

## Where the profits go

::: {.custom-style style="font-size: 1.6em;"}
Excess earnings are remitted to the U.S. Treasury.
:::

## Already audited

Annual external audits.

Weekly balance sheet.

Testimony and a Monetary Policy Report to Congress.

## Independent agencies more generally

The Fed is the vivid case of a broader American pattern: some tasks are hard to do well if every decision is a campaign issue.

## Texas note

Texas also uses specialized commissions rather than one statewide executive for some high-stakes economic regulation.

The Railroad Commission is the local illustration of insulated economic administration — not a second Fed.

## The standing trade-off

Insulation can protect long-term goods.

Insulation can also hide mistakes and weaken democratic control.

## Recap

- Credible commitment is an institution, not a slogan
- The Fed is a designed hybrid: public goals, insulated means
- Conspiracy stories usually start from a grain of truth and then skip the statute
- Independence is a trade-off, not a magic shield

## Top Hat

- T/F: Excess earnings of the Federal Reserve are remitted to the U.S. Treasury.
- MC: The Fed’s dual mandate is best summarized as:
- T/F: The Federal Reserve is a purely private bank owned by foreign families.
- Likert: “Interest rates should be set directly by elected officials.”
